nom: CeraVe Skin Renewing Vitamin C Serum

segments.oily: One reviewer with oily/combination skin reports the serum fits well into a routine without added issues, though CeraVe's own product description warns of possible breakouts for oily, breakout-prone skin.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin report the serum is hydrating and improves texture and glow without the dryness or irritation they experienced with other vitamin C products, though one notes it can feel drying and requires extra moisturizer.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination (including combination-dry) skin report light texture, easy spreading and hydration, though one with pale combination-dry, sensitive skin reports visible orange discoloration near the hairline.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin (including eczema-prone) generally report no irritation, fading bumps, and improved tone, calling it one of the few vitamin C serums that doesn't sting or trigger breakouts.
segments.mature: Reviewers describing mature or older skin (40s–70s) report visible brightening, smoothing, plumping and fading of age spots with consistent use.
segments.normal: One reviewer describing generally good/normal skin reports no pilling and a smooth, non-greasy application when layered under moisturizer.

concerns.aging: Reviewers using it for fine lines and mature-skin concerns report softened lines, plumper and smoother skin, and a general youthful glow; one reviewer in her 40s reports no fine lines developing while using it long-term.
concerns.dehydration: Many reviewers report increased hydration, plumpness and dewiness, including some with dry skin who had struggled with other vitamin C products; one reviewer notes the product seemed to dry out her skin, requiring extra moisturizer.
concerns.redness: One reviewer with sun-damaged, fair skin reports reduced red spots and bumps on the forehead, though some mild redness persisted.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer with sensitive skin reports the serum helped rather than hurt her skin barrier, describing it as hydrating and nourishing.
concerns.spots: Most reviewers using it for dark spots, hyperpigmentation or sun spots report fading and more even tone over weeks to months; a few report no visible change and one reports the product itself turning her skin orange rather than fading marks.
concerns.blemishes: Several reviewers report fading acne scarring and fewer breakouts over time; one reviewer reports small bumps appearing initially that resolved with continued use, and CeraVe's own listing warns oily, acne-prone users may see increased breakouts.
concerns.oiliness: Only one reviewer with oily/combination skin discusses it, reporting it fits into her routine without adding excess oil or issues.

aspects.libelle: Orange staining on pale or olive skin

extraits.texte: Sadly this didnt work for me. I've been using it twice a day since December 29, 2024. I haven't noticed my skin brighten at all nor has my sister notifed a difference either. I did develop some tiny small bumps when I first applied to my face, but they quickly went away the more I used it. It does apply on smooth. I put it own before my moisturizer. I was hoping to brighten areas on my face where I have Hyperpigmentation and acne scars. I'm also an African American woman if thst helps.

I have combination to dry, sensitive skin and have been using this vitamin C serum in the morning for a few weeks. I like that it feels light and has a serum-like texture that spreads easily, making it comfortable to wear. I usually follow up with other products to seal it in, which helps my skin feel hydrated throughout the day. The biggest issue for me, as someone with very pale skin, is that the serum causes certain areas to turn orange after a few hours. This usually happens near my hairline and eyebrows and is very noticeable, almost like smudges of food on my face. I have tried using only a tiny amount, patting it on instead of spreading, and even avoiding those areas, but the discoloration still appears. That said, after using it consistently for a while, I have noticed that my skin looks more radiant and has a healthy glow. Additionally, the serum comes in a convenient squeeze tube, though sometimes the first bit is already slightly oxidized, which feels wasteful (I might try storing it in the fridge). Overall, the serum works well, but the visible orange tint on pale skin is a major drawback.

My favorite Cerave product - I have tried so many things from them and this is the inly thing I'm sticking with!! My first ever Vitamin C serum and I went with this one because I heard it's a good option for sensitive skin but still potent to help with acne scars. I did not expect this to be SO hydrating. My face is a lot less dull, my acne scars are reducing - not completely gone but def a lot better from before I started this product. Ever since I started this serum I feel like I have found my skin care routine that even though I'd love to try other products I'm just scared I would miss this. I will 100% be repurchasing and maybeee trying another vitaminC serum in the future. My favorite thing about this serum is that even though I have sensitive skin this serum is so hydrating and nourishing for my skin that it even helped with my skin barrier. The change in brightness, scars, etc is very light but also I haven't even finished the first container yet. I'm really happy with this product and can't wait to see the results of using it for a couple more months!!

I'm 29 years old and decided I needed a skincare regimen. I have dry, sensitive skin, and wanted to start an anti-aging skincare regimen. I tried another brands skincare products, and after prolonged use, I was breaking out with little bumps (not acne) on my cheeks. I knew I needed something for sensitive skin. I used the Cerave quiz and went and bought what they recommended. This is just one of the recommended products... After the first night of using Cerave, the little bumps were already disappearing! After a few rounds of using the recommended skincare from Cerave, I notice my dark circles are lighter! If you have sensitive skin, look no further than the Cerave brand, no matter how many products are recommended to you by people you know. Cerave truly is for sensitive skin, and it has saved my skin, and it's also doing the job I wanted for my skin in the very beginning.

As someone with mature skin, finding a serum that truly delivers on its promises is like discovering a hidden treasure. From the moment I incorporated this serum into my skincare routine, my skin felt like it had sipped from the fountain of youth. The glow it imparts is nothing short of magical. Fine lines appear softened, and my complexion radiates vitality. The intense hydration leaves my face plump, dewy, and oh-so-touchable. It's like a spa day in a bottle.Dark spots and uneven tone? Sayonara! With consistent use, my skin looks more even, and those pesky age spots are fading away. It's like Photoshop for real life. My skin texture has undergone a delightful makeover. Pores appear minimized, and the overall canvas feels smoother. Makeup glides on effortlessly, and I'm one step closer to that flawless finish.

For someone with dry skin, it has been really hard to find a vitamin C product that doesn't dry out and irritate my skin. This is the only one I found that I actually like, and I see a real difference in the texture and overall tone of my skin. It's also fairly priced. I like it so much that I felt like I had to spread the gospel after seeing the negative reviews here. It also lays nicely under makeup for me, I apply it in the morning and then proceed with my routine and haven't had any issues.

My dermatologist recommended Cerave Skin Renewing Vitamin C to minimize facial dark spots. After using once a day for two months I did notice improvement in diminishing dark spots. A small amount of product goes a long way. I liked the fragrance and texture. It can be used under makeup. This product seems to dry out your skin so I added additional moisturizer.
